newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha firmer on crude gains on ACCESS.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha firmer on crude gains on ACCESS.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha picked up in afternoon trade on Friday, supported by firmer crude prices on the ACCESS after-hours trading system, traders said.
Open-spec naphtha for second-half December was assessed at $215.00/$216.00, up from $214.00/$215.00 in late Thursday trade.
First-half January was indicated about $1.00 lower than the second-half December level.
In inter-delivery naphtha spreads, second-half December/second-half January was notionally quoted at plus $1.75, compared with Thursday's plus $1.50.

In middle distillates, kerosene importers shifted their attention from second-half November to December delivery cargoes, traders said. They said trading houses were likely to import kerosene cargoes toward the winter just to secure market share even if the imported cargoes end up costing more at the wholesale level than domestic cargoes.

Japan's kerosene stocks in September grew 8.7 percent from a year ago to 4.76 million kilolitres (kl), the Ministry of International Trade and Industry said. Naphtha stocks totalled 1.76 million kl, up 10.3 percent from a year earlier.
